atlas-at.0113: Negotiation is expected: karriere.at gives a typical raise of 10 to 20% on a job change and 5 to 10% at entry level, and advises asking for a range and justifying it by qualifications, not by personal costs.
atlas-at.0114: The graduate files the Red-White-Red Card application, not the employer: no labour market test for graduates of Austrian universities, a work contract and an employer’s declaration from the firm, and pay at the level of comparable Austrian junior graduates. A 12-month extension of the student permit covers the job search.
atlas-at.0115: Employers that hire foreign graduates are the large ones with international pools; the state talent portal Work in Austria offers help with residence and work questions after a job offer.
atlas-at.0116: What an employer wants to hear is your permit status and the date it ends, early, before the contract is drafted: say whether you hold a student permit or the job-search extension and when you could start.
atlas-at.0117: Official: the AMS (ams.at) with MeinAMS and the "alle jobs" search engine; the Work in Austria Talent Hub for foreign professionals; federal jobs on jobboerse.gv.at, reached from oeffentlicherdienst.gv.at.
atlas-at.0118: Boards and fairs: karriere.at for job ads and application guides; Career Calling in Vienna, the TECONOMY series and university career days (see Events); the WU ZBP Career Center for internships and first jobs.
atlas-at.0119: Employer pages: erstegroup.com/en/career/graduates, the voestalpine job portal, Deloitte Austria’s portal and BCG’s Visiting Associate page.
atlas-at.0120: Waiting for a trainee advert: voestalpine says its trainee programmes are offered "whenever required" and it also takes unsolicited applications after graduation, so send an Initiativbewerbung as well.
atlas-at.0121: Missing the student-job window: voestalpine’s holiday-job applications close at the end of January, with notice of openings by the end of May, so autumn is too late.
atlas-at.0122: Quoting net pay, one figure or 12 payments: give a gross annual range with 14 payments.
atlas-at.0123: Thinking a foreign degree must be nostrified for every job: it is for regulated professions; for other jobs an ENIC NARIC assessment is an optional addition, and for regulated ones an assessment is not enough.
atlas-at.0124: McKinsey’s recruiters say fluent German is mandatory for its Germany and Austria offices; BCG’s second round has one case in German and one in English, and documents may be in either language.
atlas-at.0125: German is often required even where English is the working language; juniors in Vienna should expect it to be asked.
atlas-at.0126: voestalpine’s High Performance Metals programme asks for very good German and English; its automotive-components trainee programme asks for excellent English.
atlas-at.0127: Deloitte Austria’s application pages are in German and name no language level or interview language; the pages read give no evidence of English-only audit hiring.
atlas-at.0128: In December 2024 the AMS unemployment rate was 3.4% for people with a university, college or teacher-training degree and 8.2% across all education levels; at the end of January 2025, 31,674 graduates were registered unemployed, 18% more than a year before.
atlas-at.0129: The AMS says vacancies asking for a degree rose from about 400 to over 5,500 on average between 1993 and 2024, but still make up only 6.1% of the vacancies reported to it.
atlas-at.0130: EU, EEA and Swiss citizens work with no labour-market authorisation.
atlas-at.0131: Register your address (Meldezettel, signed by your landlord) within three working days of moving in; it is free.
atlas-at.0132: Staying over three months, apply for the registration certificate (Anmeldebescheinigung, €44) within four months, with your work contract or, for students, enrolment, means and full health cover.
atlas-at.0134: Apply at an Austrian embassy; immigration (MA 35 in Vienna) decides and the consulate issues a D visa to collect the card. Work up to 20 hours a week with an employment-service permit, given without a labour-market test.
atlas-at.0135: To renew each year, show at least 16 ECTS credits from the previous year. A non-EU student with a permit from another EU country can study here up to 360 days on the university’s notification.
atlas-at.0142: €218 permit, plus €195 for the D visa
atlas-at.0145: If your rent exceeds €386.43 a month, the difference must be covered by extra funds on top of the monthly amount.
atlas-at.0147: An internship your study plan requires needs no work permit, but non-EU interns must be notified by the employer to the employment service (AMS) at least two weeks before they start; pay follows the collective agreement.
atlas-at.0148: An unpaid “Volontariat” may last at most three months a year: calling a working intern a volunteer is illegal employment, with fines of €1,000 to €10,000.
atlas-at.0149: Twelve months to look for work after an Austrian degree
atlas-at.0150: After a bachelor’s, master’s or PhD in Austria, extend your student permit by 12 months, once, applying before it expires.
atlas-at.0151: A job suited to your degree then gets a Red-White-Red Card for graduates, applied for inside Austria, with no points and no labour-market test, at the collective-agreement pay.
atlas-at.0154: Job-seeker visa for very highly qualified people
atlas-at.0155: With at least 70 of 100 points for degree, experience, languages and age, you can get a six-month D visa to look for work, then apply for the card in Austria once you have an offer.
atlas-at.0157: A 24-month card tied to one employer, with five routes: very highly qualified (70 points, no labour test), shortage occupations (55 points, no labour test), other key workers (55 points and a salary floor, with a labour test), graduates of Austrian universities (no points, no test) and start-up founders.
atlas-at.0158: After 21 months of qualified work in 24 you move to the Red-White-Red Card Plus, which opens the whole labour market.
atlas-at.0160: €3,465 a month (€48,510 a year with 13th and 14th)
atlas-at.0162: Language certificates count only from ÖSD, Goethe, telc or ÖIF (German) or Cambridge, IELTS, TOEFL or TOEIC (English), and only within 12 months of the application.
atlas-at.0164: A contract of at least six months and a three-year degree, or for IT three years of experience in the last seven; no points.
atlas-at.0166: €55,678 a year (€3,977 a month over 14 payments)
atlas-at.0168: A hosting agreement with an accredited research body; no employment-service permit, no visa fee, and 12 more months after the research to find work or start a company.
atlas-at.0169: A PhD on a university contract comes as a researcher with full social security; one on a scholarship comes as a student, and the scholarship is free of income tax.
atlas-at.0170: US citizens aged 18 to 30 can get a working-holiday D visa for 6 or 12 months from the embassy; work is secondary, and the visa cannot be renewed or converted in Austria.
atlas-at.0171: Austria has no working-holiday agreement with the UK.
atlas-at.0172: Only for citizens of Argentina, Australia, Canada, Chile, South Korea, Japan, Hong Kong, Israel, New Zealand and Taiwan aged 18 to 30 (35 for Canada).
atlas-at.0174: Up to 90 days in any 180, with no work. Visa-free nationals may file a first application inside Austria, but filing does not extend the 90 days.
atlas-at.0176: Choose housing whose landlord or manager will countersign the registration form (Meldezettel): without registration you cannot open a bank account or collect a residence card. Student residences sign it at once.
atlas-at.0177: Documents issued outside the EU need an apostille or full legalisation, and German translations by a court-registered translator (Gerichtsdolmetscher).
atlas-at.0178: Apply at the Austrian embassy or consulate for where you live; once the immigration office approves, it issues a D visa, valid up to 90 days, to travel and collect the permit.
atlas-at.0179: Register at the registration office (Meldeamt) within 3 working days of moving in, with the form countersigned by your landlord. It is free, and you get the confirmation of registration on the spot.
atlas-at.0180: Staying more than 3 months, apply for a registration certificate (Anmeldebescheinigung) within 4 months of arriving: €44, with proof of work, or for students enrolment, funds and full health cover. Missing the deadline can be fined up to €250.
atlas-at.0181: Collect the residence permit card in person at the immigration office (in Vienna, MA 35), where your fingerprints are taken and the flat fee is paid. In Vienna, waits of 4 to 12 months are common; outside it, 4 to 8 weeks.
atlas-at.0182: Your 10-digit social security number (SVNR) is assigned when your employer or the health fund ÖGK registers you. A tax number comes from the tax office (Finanzamt).
atlas-at.0183: Without an Austrian biometric document, your health card (e-card) is not printed until you register a photo in person at a police office or ÖGK centre; until then, ask for a paper treatment certificate (Behandlungsbeleg).
atlas-at.0184: Students not covered by work or family can insure themselves with ÖGK for €78.84 a month in 2026.
atlas-at.0185: EU students show their European Health Insurance Card, or private cover, for the registration certificate.
